0.0.n: ということ forms a set phrase that introduces a conclusion or transition.

0.1.n: こと means a matter or situation; here it helps build the transition ということで.

0.2.n: で completes ということで, linking the preceding situation to this wrap-up.

0.3.n: です adds a polite tone here rather than a separate statement.

0.4.n: ね gently draws the listener in and gives the speaker a moment to continue.

0.7.n: カヴェルナ is the name of the board game being unboxed.

0.9.n: の links the game title to 開封動画, identifying what the video unboxes.

0.10.n: ですね interrupts the noun phrase as a conversational pause; it does not describe the game.

0.11.n: ね is part of the filler ですね before the speaker continues with 開封動画.

0.13.n: 開封 means opening packaging and modifies 動画 here.

0.14.n: 動画 combines with 開封 to name the kind of video presented.

0.15.n: を marks 開封動画 as what the speaker presented.

0.16.n: お届け combines with しました to politely describe bringing content to viewers.

0.17.n: しました is the polite past form of する, completing お届けしました.

0.18.n: けども softly connects this recap to what comes next, without requiring a strong contrast.

1.0.n: まあ is a conversational filler that softens the transition to the next topic.

1.1.n: これ points to the game or its components currently under discussion.

1.2.n: です adds politeness to the conversational phrase これですね.

1.3.n: ね invites the listener to follow the speaker's reference to the game.

1.5.n: 実際 shifts attention from the unboxing to the practical steps that follow.

1.6.n: あと refers to the remaining things to do after the unboxing.

1.7.n: は marks あと as the topic: what remains to be done.

1.8.n: この must come before a noun; with 後 it refers to the time following this.

1.9.n: 後 combines with この to mean after this, referring to the next stage.

1.10.n: 切り抜く becomes 切り抜いて plus みて, meaning to try the action; the final て links to the next step.

2.0.n: プレイ is a borrowed word used for playing a game.

2.1.n: の links プレイ to 準備, specifying what the preparations are for.

2.2.n: 準備 combines with をする to describe getting things ready.

2.3.n: を marks 準備 as the thing being done.

2.4.n: してみて means try doing and links onward; です belongs to the spoken filler ですね, not the verb form.

2.5.n: ね completes the polite filler ですね between the planned actions.

2.7.n: また points ahead to another occasion when the speaker may play and discuss the game.

2.8.n: プレイ combines with できる to express being able to play the game.

2.9.n: できたら is the if-form of できる; the attached です belongs to the filler ですね.

2.10.n: ね completes a conversational pause after the condition, before the speaker states the intended action.

3.0.n: ご adds respect; 紹介してみたい combines introducing, trying it, and wanting to do so.

3.1.n: と marks the preceding wish as the content of 思います.

3.2.n: 思います is polite; after たいと, it gently expresses an intention or wish.

4.0.n: はい signals the start of the closing sign-off rather than answering a question.

4.2.n: This is the first part of the channel name The Game Gallery.

4.4.n: This is part of the channel name The Game Gallery, not a separate Japanese word.

4.6.n: This completes the channel name The Game Gallery.

4.7.n: の links the channel name to its presenter, showing affiliation.

4.8.n: HAL is the first part of the presenter's handle, HAL99.

4.9.n: These digits complete the presenter's handle HAL99; they are not a count here.

4.10.n: でし is the stem used before た in でした, the polite past form of です.

4.11.n: た completes でした, a conventional way to identify oneself when signing off.

4.13.n: では introduces the farewell and signals that the video is ending.

4.14.n: また pairs with 次回 in a farewell that leaves see you understood.

4.15.n: 次回 refers to the next video or installment.

0.lit: So, you see, we presented Caverna's unboxing video, though...
0.tip: The repeated ですね phrases are polite conversational fillers; they do not change the main message.

1.lit: Well, this, you see, actually, as for what remains, after this, try punching out...
1.tip: A verb's て-form plus みる means to try doing it, not to watch it.

2.lit: Try making preparations for play, you see, and later, if I can play, you see...
2.tip: できたら means if I can; its past-looking form expresses a future condition here.

3.lit: I think I would like to try introducing it.
3.tip: たいと思います softens a wish into a polite statement of intention.

4.lit: All right, this was HAL99 of The Game Gallery. Well then, again next time!
4.tip: でした is commonly used in closing self-identifications, like English this was, even though the speaker is still present.
